lessons.title: The three categories of Tawheed
objectives: Define Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah, al-Uluhiyyah and al-Asma was-Sifat
Give a Qur'anic evidence for each
Explain why Uluhiyyah is the message of every prophet

keywords.def: Allah alone creates, owns and controls all things
Allah alone is worshipped
believing in Allah's names and attributes as He described Himself

starter: Name three names of Allah with meanings.

teach.heading: Why divide Tawheed?
bullets: Scholars studied the Qur'an and Sunnah
They found three areas of Tawheed
It helps us understand and teach belief
teach.note: Bismillah. Explain that the three categories are an organised way to understand what the Qur'an teaches, as scholars of ahl as-sunnah have done. They are not separate beliefs; they work together. Draw a triangle on the board.

teach.heading: Rububiyyah: Lordship
bullets: Allah alone creates, owns and runs the universe
teach.note: 7:54: His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds. Ask: what do you depend on that Allah controls? Even the idolaters of Makkah admitted Allah created the heavens and earth (29:61).

teach.heading: Uluhiyyah: worship
bullets: Prayer, dua, trust, sacrifice for Allah alone
This was the message of all prophets
teach.note: 51:56 and 16:36. The Makkans accepted Rububiyyah but still worshipped idols; therefore the Prophet ﷺ called them to Uluhiyyah. Ask: why is it not enough to say Allah is Creator? Because worship belongs to Him alone.

teach.heading: Asma was-Sifat
bullets: Allah has perfect names and attributes
42:11: nothing is like Him, He hears and sees
teach.note: Recap Year 4. Keep it to the method: affirm what Allah and His Messenger affirmed, without likening Him to creation, without denying, without asking how, without distorting meanings. Mention 20:5 as an example.

teach.heading: Put it together
bullets: Names lead to love and awe
teach.note: Give a quick example: knowing that Allah alone provides (Rububiyyah) means we only ask Him (Uluhiyyah), and knowing He hears (Names) means we make dua. Pairs complete a diagram.

practice: Why do we make dua to Allah only?
independent: Create a table: category / definition / evidence / example
Write a paragraph: why did Quraysh need to be called to Uluhiyyah?
Match statements to the category
exit: Which category was denied by the idol worshippers of Makkah in practice?
lessons.homework: Explain the three categories of Tawheed to a family member using one example each.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: three-column organiser with sentence frames. Stretch: explain why a Muslim cannot accept Rububiyyah without Uluhiyyah.

lessons.title: Tawheed in action: dua, trust and reliance
objectives: Explain that dua is worship
Explain tawakkul and its balance with effort
Explain why we direct worship only to Allah

keywords.def: calling on Allah in worship and need
relying on Allah while taking the means
seeking help in distress

starter: Name the three categories of Tawheed.
Who do we call on in dua?

teach.heading: Dua is worship
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said: dua is worship
Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud (an-Nu'man ibn Bashir)
Allah says: call upon Me, I will respond (40:60)
teach.note: Bismillah. Read the hadith and 40:60. Ask: why is dua called worship? Because it shows need and trust in Allah. Link to Uluhiyyah.

teach.heading: Ask Allah
bullets: If you seek help, seek help from Allah
teach.note: Read the hadith. Clarify: it is permissible to seek help from people in what they are able to do (e.g. a doctor). What is forbidden is asking creation for what only Allah can give. 27:62: He answers the distressed one.

teach.heading: Tawakkul
bullets: Trust Allah and take the means
5:23: rely on Allah if you are believers
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said to the man who left his camel untied and said he trusted Allah: tie it, then trust (Tirmidhi, hasan). Ask: what does this show? Tawakkul is not laziness.

teach.heading: Stories
bullets: Musa at the sea: My Lord is with me
teach.note: Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil was said by Ibrahim in the fire and by the Prophet ﷺ when told people had gathered against them (Bukhari, Ibn Abbas). Musa: 'Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me' (26:62). Link to tawakkul.

teach.heading: Our daily Tawheed
teach.note: Pairs write a list of everyday situations where they will ask Allah: exams, journeys, illness. Share. Encourage pupils to speak to Allah in their own words and to begin with Bismillah and end with Alhamdulillah.

practice: What do we say at the beginning?
independent: Write a dua for a difficult situation
Explain the camel hadith in your own words
Complete: Tawheed in action is when I ______
exit: What is the balance in tawakkul?
lessons.homework: Make dua daily for a week for something important and keep a short log.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with sentence frames. Stretch: write a reflection on the balance of trust and effort.

lessons.title: Belief in Qadar: Allah's decree
objectives: Define Qadar and its four levels
Explain that humans have choice and responsibility
Explain how Qadar brings comfort

keywords.def: Allah's knowledge, writing, will and creation of all things
choice and intention
what Allah has ordained

starter: Name the six pillars of iman.

teach.heading: The sixth pillar
bullets: Believe in Qadar, good and bad
teach.note: Bismillah. Recall the hadith of Jibril. Qur'an 54:49: indeed We created all things with qadar. Ask: why is it hard to understand? Remind that we accept what Allah told us.

teach.heading: Four levels
teach.note: Level 1, 'Ilm: Allah knows what was and will be (22:70). Level 2, Kitabah: everything is written. Level 3, Mashi'ah: nothing happens except by Allah's will (81:29). Level 4, Khalq: Allah created all things including our acts (37:96).

teach.heading: We choose
bullets: Allah gave us will and choice
teach.note: Qur'an 18:29: say the truth is from your Lord; whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve. Our choices are real, and are within Allah's knowledge and will. Do not use Qadar as an excuse for sin.

teach.heading: Effort and Qadar
teach.note: Muslim (Abu Hurairah): the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak one, yet in both there is good. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah's help and do not give up. If something befalls you do not say 'if only'; say 'Qadar Allah wa ma sha'a fa'al'.

teach.heading: Comfort
bullets: What missed you was not meant to hit you
teach.note: Know that what missed you was never going to befall you, and what befell you was never going to miss you (Tirmidhi, from the advice to Ibn Abbas). Ask: how can this reduce worry? Link to patience and gratitude.

practice: What does 'effort' have to do with faith?
independent: Explain the four levels in a table with an evidence for each
Write a reflection: how does Qadar reduce worry?
Answer: can we blame Qadar for sin? Explain.
exit: Give a verse about human choice.
lessons.homework: Discuss with family one hard event and how belief in Qadar helps; write a paragraph.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: four-level diagram with pictures. Stretch: write a short explanation of why choice and Qadar do not contradict.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Ta'if, Isra and Mi'raj, and sawm
lessons.title: The Year of Sorrow
lessons.bigQuestion: When something really sad happens, what helps a person keep going?
objectives: To understand what the Prophet ﷺ faced in the Year of Sorrow and how he responded with patience
successCriteria: All: name the two people he lost in the Year of Sorrow
Most: describe the boycott before it
Some: explain what sabr looked like for him
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: patience and hope in hard times

keywords.def: the year Abu Talib and Khadijah died
refusing to trade, marry or mix with a group
patience: staying firm and trusting Allah
the uncle who protected the Prophet ﷺ

hook.text: When something really sad happens, what helps a person keep going?
hook.a: Trust in Allah, du'a, patience and people who care.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease' (ash-Sharh 94:5-6).

starter.q: Who were the first four Muslims?
Where was the first revelation?
Which hill did he call from publicly?
What does sabr mean?

teach.heading: The boycott
bullets: Quraysh stopped trading with the Muslims
Banu Hashim stayed in a valley
teach.note: Explain the boycott simply: an agreement hung in the Ka'bah. The Muslims and the Prophet's ﷺ clan suffered hunger until it ended.

teach.heading: Two great losses
teach.note: Ask: why were these two people so important to him?

left.title: Abu Talib
points: Cared for him since age eight

teach.heading: Patience and trust
bullets: He made du'a and kept praying
teach.note: Link to Allah's promise: 'For indeed, with hardship comes ease' (ash-Sharh 94:5). Hardship is not a sign Allah has left us.

check.q: Why is it called the Year of Sorrow?
check.why: It was the year he lost both his protector and his beloved wife.

practice.q: Explain why the Year of Sorrow was so hard for him.
practice.a: He lost Abu Talib, who protected him, and Khadijah, who supported him, soon after the boycott.
practice.model: First he lost Abu Talib, so Quraysh could harm him more. Then Khadijah died, his support at home. This came right after years of boycott.

practice.q: How long did the boycott last?
practice.a: About three years

practice.q: Give one way he showed sabr.
practice.a: He kept praying and calling people to Allah.

independent.q: Write a short paragraph in the portal response box: 'How the Prophet ﷺ showed sabr in the Year of Sorrow'. Start: 'In the Year of Sorrow ...'
independent.a: For example: In the Year of Sorrow he lost Abu Talib and Khadijah. He was very sad but kept praying, making du'a and calling people to Allah.
independent.model: Teacher models: 'In the Year of Sorrow, the Prophet ﷺ lost two people he loved. Even so, he ...' and finishes with one example.

independent.q: Extend: what does 94:5 promise people who are patient?
independent.a: That with hardship comes ease.

independent.q: Stretch: how can we support a friend who is sad?
independent.a: Listen, make du'a for them, help them, remind them of Allah's mercy.

exit.q: Who protected the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah until the Year of Sorrow?
exit.a: Abu Talib

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what helped the Prophet ﷺ keep going?
exit.a: Trust in Allah, prayer and patience.

lessons.homework: Learn ash-Sharh 94:5-6 with its meaning and share it with someone who is having a hard time.
lessons.send: SEND: two-column picture card (Abu Talib, Khadijah) with places, not people. EAL: paragraph frame. Stretch: link sabr to qadar.

Exercise book

pictures.alt: Al-Mu'alla in Makkah, where Khadijah is buried
Sunrise after the night: ease after hardship

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Ta'if, Isra and Mi'raj, and sawm
lessons.title: Isra and Mi'raj: the gift of the five prayers
lessons.bigQuestion: If you received a gift straight from the King of all kings, how would you look after it?
objectives: To understand the events of the Isra and Mi'raj and why salah is a special gift
successCriteria: All: describe the Isra from Makkah to Jerusalem
Most: describe the Mi'raj and the gift of salah
Some: explain why Abu Bakr was called as-Siddiq
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: valuing salah as Allah's gift

keywords.def: the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem
the rising up through the heavens
the masjid in Jerusalem
the one who always believes the truth: Abu Bakr

hook.text: If you received a gift straight from the King of all kings, how would you look after it?
hook.a: With great care. Salah was given to us directly on the Mi'raj.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa' (al-Isra 17:1).

starter.q: Where is Ta'if?
What did the Prophet ﷺ choose at Ta'if?
Who died in the Year of Sorrow?
Name the five daily prayers.

teach.heading: The Isra
bullets: From Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa
He led the prophets in prayer
teach.note: Al-Isra 17:1 describes the journey. Muslim reports he led the prophets in prayer at al-Aqsa. Never draw or show the Buraq or the Prophet ﷺ.

quote.text: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs.

teach.heading: The Mi'raj
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim report he met prophets including Adam, Isa, Yusuf, Musa and Ibrahim (peace be upon them).

teach.heading: From fifty to five
teach.note: Tell it in steps: 50 prayers given; Musa advised asking for less; reduced to 5 with the reward of 50.

model.problem: How many prayers were first given, and what reward do the five carry?
steps: Musa advised asking to make them fewer
Five prayers carry the reward of fifty
model.answer: Five prayers a day, with the reward of fifty

teach.heading: As-Siddiq
bullets: Abu Bakr said: if he said it, it is true
teach.note: Commonly reported in the seerah. Ask: why did Abu Bakr believe straight away?

check.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ bring back from the Mi'raj?
check.why: Salah was made obligatory on that night. Fasting and Hajj came later.

practice.q: Explain the difference between Isra and Mi'raj.
practice.a: Isra: night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem. Mi'raj: rising through the heavens.
practice.model: Isra is the journey across the earth: Makkah to Jerusalem. Mi'raj is the rising up: through the heavens. Both happened in one night.

practice.q: How many prayers were first given?
practice.a: Fifty

practice.q: Why was Abu Bakr called as-Siddiq?
practice.a: He believed the Prophet ﷺ immediately.

independent.q: Complete a two-part journey diagram labelled Isra and Mi'raj, with three facts for each.
independent.a: Isra: Makkah, Jerusalem, led prophets in prayer. Mi'raj: seven heavens, met prophets, gift of salah.
independent.model: Teacher draws an arrow from Makkah to Jerusalem and writes 'Isra: one night'.

independent.q: Extend: what does the reduction from fifty to five teach us about Allah?
independent.a: He is merciful and makes the religion easy.

independent.q: Stretch: how should knowing salah's story change how we pray?
independent.a: We value it as a gift and pray on time with focus.

exit.q: The Isra ended at ...
exit.a: Masjid al-Aqsa

exit.q: Back to our ponder: how will you look after the gift of salah?
exit.a: For example: pray on time with focus.

lessons.homework: Pray each salah on time for three days and tick it on a chart; tell the class which was hardest.
lessons.send: SEND: two-arrow journey diagram ready to label. EAL: key word cards with Arabic. Stretch: explain the link between al-Aqsa and earlier prophets.

School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Mushaf or printed al-Isra 17:1

lessons.unit: Spring 2: The pledges at Aqabah, the Hijrah and zakah
lessons.title: The pledges at Aqabah and the Ansar
lessons.bigQuestion: Why might people from another town believe a message that a messenger's own people rejected?
objectives: To understand how the pledges at Aqabah prepared the way for the Hijrah to Madinah
successCriteria: All: say who the Ansar were
Most: explain what was promised at the two pledges
Some: explain why the pledges were a turning point
lessons.smsc: Moral: keeping promises; Social: a community welcoming others

keywords.def: a pledge: a solemn promise of loyalty
a place near Mina, outside Makkah
the helpers: the Muslims of Madinah
the old name of Madinah

hook.text: Why might people from another town believe a message that a messenger's own people rejected?
hook.a: They heard it with open hearts and saw the truth; Allah guided them.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And fulfil every promise. Indeed, the promise will be questioned about' (al-Isra 17:34).

starter.q: Bismillah. Zakat al-fitr is given before ...
Where did the Isra end?
Which town rejected the Prophet ﷺ in the Year of Sorrow?

teach.heading: Visitors from Yathrib
bullets: Pilgrims came to Makkah each year
The Prophet ﷺ spoke to people from Yathrib
Some believed and took the message home
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Dates from the seerah are approximate.

teach.heading: Two pledges
teach.note: Compare the two pledges.

head: Pledge
Who and when
What they promised
rows: To worship Allah alone, not steal, not slander, obey in good
To protect the Prophet ﷺ as their own families

teach.heading: A teacher is sent
bullets: Mus'ab ibn Umayr went to Yathrib
He taught the Qur'an and Islam
Many homes in Yathrib became Muslim
teach.note: Reported in the seerah.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What did the second pledge add?
options: A promise to protect the Prophet ﷺ
check.why: The second pledge promised protection, preparing for the Hijrah.

practice.q: Explain why the pledges at Aqabah were a turning point.
practice.a: The people of Yathrib promised to believe and protect the Prophet ﷺ, so the Muslims had a safe home to migrate to.
practice.model: Point: the pledges gave the Muslims a new home. Evidence: at the second pledge they promised to protect the Prophet ﷺ. Explain: after Ta'if rejected him, Yathrib welcomed Islam. Link: this opened the way to the Hijrah.

practice.q: Who was sent to teach in Yathrib?
practice.a: Mus'ab ibn Umayr

practice.q: Ansar means ...
practice.a: Helpers

independent.q: Write the two pledges as a 'promise scroll' on the pupil PDF: who, when, and three promises, then one sentence on why they mattered.
independent.a: Accurate who and when, promises, and why it mattered
independent.model: Teacher fills the first scroll: 'First pledge, about 621 CE, 12 people: we promise to worship Allah alone ...'

independent.q: Extend: why do you think the people of Yathrib were ready to listen?
independent.a: They wanted peace and guidance; they had heard of a coming prophet; Allah guided them.

independent.q: Stretch: what makes a promise serious in Islam?
independent.a: Allah asks us to keep promises; a pledge is a trust (amanah).

exit.q: The Ansar were from ...
exit.a: Yathrib (Madinah)

exit.q: Back to our ponder: why did the people of Yathrib believe?
exit.a: They listened with open hearts and Allah guided them.

lessons.homework: Tell your family about one promise from the pledge that we can still keep today.
lessons.send: SEND: scroll with gaps and a word bank. EAL: who / when / what table. Stretch: compare Ta'if's response with Yathrib's.

School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: promise scrolls

lessons.unit: Spring 2: The pledges at Aqabah, the Hijrah and zakah
lessons.title: Zakah: meaning, purpose and the idea of nisab
lessons.bigQuestion: Can giving money away make your wealth grow? How?
objectives: To understand what zakah is, why Allah commands it and how nisab decides who pays
successCriteria: All: say that zakah is the third pillar of Islam
Most: explain the meaning of zakah and its purpose
Some: work out zakah at 2.5% on an example amount above nisab
lessons.smsc: Moral: generosity and caring for the poor

keywords.def: a set part of savings given each year to those in need
make clean
the minimum amount of wealth before zakah is due
two and a half pounds in every hundred

hook.text: Can giving money away make your wealth grow? How?
hook.a: Yes: Allah blesses and purifies wealth when zakah is given.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to increase' (at-Tawbah 9:103).

starter.q: Bismillah. The first masjid was built at ...
What year was the Hijrah?
Zakat al-fitr is given in ...

teach.heading: The third pillar
bullets: It is a right of the poor in our wealth
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Allah says: 'Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them' (at-Tawbah 9:103).

teach.heading: Who pays?
bullets: A Muslim with savings above nisab
Kept for one full Islamic year
teach.note: Nisab is often given as the value of 85 g of gold or 595 g of silver; the masjid gives the current figure. Keep amounts as examples.

teach.heading: Model: working out zakah
teach.note: Example figures only; no interest involved.

model.problem: Example: Amina's savings are £2,000, above nisab, for a full year. How much zakah?

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What is the rate of zakah on savings?

practice.q: Explain two purposes of zakah.
practice.a: It purifies the giver's wealth and heart from greed; it helps the poor and needy.
practice.model: Point: zakah purifies. Evidence: 9:103 says it purifies them. Explain: it cleans the heart from greed. Second: it is a right of the poor, so it helps those in need. Link: the whole community is cared for.

practice.q: Work out zakah on £400 (example, above nisab).
Nisab is ...
practice.a: The minimum wealth before zakah is due
options: The minimum wealth before zakah is due

independent.q: Zakah calculator on the pupil PDF (example amounts): work out 2.5% of £1,000, £3,000 and £600, then write one sentence on why zakah is a pillar.
independent.a: £25, £75, £15; zakah is a pillar because Allah commands it and it cares for the poor
independent.model: Teacher works the first: 1% of £1,000 = £10, so 2.5% = £25.

independent.q: Extend: why must the wealth be kept a full year?
independent.a: Zakah is a yearly duty on savings that have stayed above nisab for a year.

independent.q: Stretch: Yusuf's savings are below nisab. Does he pay zakah? Can he still give?
independent.a: No zakah is due, but he can give sadaqah.

exit.q: Zakah is the ... pillar of Islam.
exit.a: Third

exit.q: Back to our ponder: can giving make wealth grow?
exit.a: Yes: Allah blesses and purifies wealth when zakah is given.

lessons.homework: Ask an adult at home how your family works out zakah, or look at your masjid's zakah guide.
lessons.send: SEND: 1% then 2.5% steps with a calculator. EAL: zakah word bank. Stretch: explain nisab with gold and silver.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Ta'if, Isra and Mi'raj, and sawm
lessons.title: Sawm: what fasting is and why we fast
lessons.bigQuestion: Why would Allah ask us to stay hungry for a whole day? What could we gain?
objectives: To understand what sawm is and why Allah made fasting in Ramadan a pillar of Islam
successCriteria: All: say what sawm is and its times
Most: give two reasons Muslims fast
Some: explain how fasting builds taqwa
lessons.smsc: Moral: self-control and empathy for the hungry

keywords.def: fasting: no food or drink from dawn to sunset
the ninth month, when Muslims fast
being aware of Allah and careful to obey Him
the meal before dawn
the meal at sunset that breaks the fast

hook.text: Why would Allah ask us to stay hungry for a whole day? What could we gain?
hook.a: Taqwa, thankfulness, care for the hungry, self-control and reward.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous' (al-Baqarah 2:183).

starter.q: How many prayers were first given on the Mi'raj?
Where did the Isra end?
Which pillar of Islam is sawm?
Who was called as-Siddiq?

teach.heading: What is sawm?
bullets: No food or drink from dawn to sunset
In Ramadan, for the whole month
Also no bad words or arguing
teach.note: Fasting begins at Fajr and ends at Maghrib. Bukhari reports that Allah has no need of the fast of someone who does not leave false speech.

teach.heading: Why we fast
teach.note: Read al-Baqarah 2:183 below. Bukhari and Muslim report: whoever fasts Ramadan with iman, hoping for reward, has past sins forgiven.

quote.text: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous.

teach.heading: A fasting day
teach.note: Walk through the day; pupils say what happens at each point.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: When does the fast end each day?
check.why: The fast is from Fajr to Maghrib.

practice.q: Explain what sawm is in one sentence.
practice.a: Sawm is not eating or drinking from dawn until sunset in Ramadan, for Allah.
practice.model: Sawm means fasting: from Fajr to Maghrib I do not eat or drink, and I keep my words good, for the sake of Allah.

practice.q: The meal before dawn is ...
practice.a: Suhoor

practice.q: Give two reasons Muslims fast.
practice.a: To obey Allah and gain taqwa; to feel for the hungry

independent.q: Make a 'Why we fast' poster with four reasons, one with the ayah 2:183.
independent.a: Obey Allah; taqwa (2:183); empathy for the hungry; forgiveness and reward.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first reason: 'Allah commanded it: fasting was decreed upon us (2:183).'

independent.q: Extend: what is taqwa?
independent.a: Being aware of Allah and careful to obey Him.

independent.q: Stretch: how can fasting help control anger?
independent.a: It trains self-control; the fasting person avoids arguing.

exit.q: Fasting is in the month of ...
exit.a: Ramadan

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what do we gain by fasting?
exit.a: Taqwa, reward, self-control and care for the hungry.

lessons.homework: Ask an adult at home about their best Ramadan memory and one tip for fasting well.
lessons.send: SEND: timeline with clock pictures. EAL: key word cards. Stretch: compare fasting with self-control in other parts of life.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: zakah, sawm and Hajj
lessons.title: Hajj: the journey to the House of Allah
objectives: Define Hajj and Umrah
Describe the main rites at an introductory level
Explain the link to Ibrahim and Ismail

keywords.def: the pilgrimage to Makkah
the sacred state with simple clothing
the plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th

teach.heading: A duty once in a lifetime
bullets: The Kaaba is the House of Allah
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 3:97: pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able. The Prophet ﷺ said it is once; more is voluntary (Muslim). Ask: what does 'able' mean? Health and wealth.

teach.heading: Ibrahim and Ismail
bullets: They raised the foundations of the Kaaba
teach.note: Read 2:127 and the dua 'Our Lord, accept from us'. Link to Year 2 story of Ibrahim. Mention Ibrahim's call to pilgrimage (22:27).

teach.heading: The main rites
teach.note: Give a simple outline: Ihram (intention and clothing), Talbiyah ('Labbayka Allahumma labbayk'), Tawaf around the Kaaba, Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, standing at Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina. Do not go into detailed fiqh differences.

teach.heading: Arafah
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said Hajj is Arafah (Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud). Ask: why is standing in dua so important? Link to dependence on Allah.

teach.heading: Reward
bullets: Hajj with no wrongdoing returns him sinless
Like the day his mother bore him
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or wrongdoing returns as the day his mother bore him. Compare Hajj and Umrah. Reflect.

independent: Draw a flowchart of the Hajj rites
Write a paragraph: why is Hajj a unifying experience?
Compare Hajj and Umrah in a table
lessons.homework: Research one rite of Hajj and prepare a one-minute explanation.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: step diagram with pictures. Stretch: link Hajj to the story of Ibrahim.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: advice, speech and truth online
lessons.title: The religion is sincere advice
objectives: State the hadith on naseehah
Explain how to give advice with adab
Explain how to accept advice

keywords.def: sincere advice
honest and wishing good
good manners

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: For Allah, His Book, His Messenger
For the leaders and the common people
teach.note: Bismillah. Muslim (Tamim ad-Dari). Read and explain each: sincerity to Allah (worship), to the Book (reading and following), to the Prophet (obeying), to leaders and Muslims (wishing good).

teach.heading: Giving advice
teach.note: Ask: how would you like to be advised? The Prophet ﷺ was gentle (Qur'an 3:159). Model a gentle approach. Avoid embarrassing.

teach.heading: Receiving advice
teach.note: Role-play: a friend says you were rude. Respond with thanks. Ibrahim said to his father: gentle words (19:42-47) · keep it simple.

teach.heading: Not naseehah
teach.note: Distinguish between sincere advice and shaming. The Prophet ﷺ said a believer is the mirror of his brother (Abu Dawud, hasan). Ask: how is a mirror helpful?

teach.heading: Practice
teach.note: Pairs rewrite harsh messages into sincere advice. Share.

independent: Rewrite three harsh comments as sincere advice
Explain the hadith for each of the five groups
Create an advice guide
exit: Give two tips for giving advice.
lessons.homework: Give sincere advice to someone at home about something good and report how it went.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with starter sentences. Stretch: write a dialogue.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: advice, speech and truth online
lessons.title: Backbiting and gossip
objectives: Define backbiting (ghibah)
Explain the Qur'anic warning and the hadith
Give strategies to avoid it

keywords.def: backbiting: mentioning something about a person that they dislike
slander: saying something false about someone
return to Allah and put things right

teach.heading: The Qur'an
bullets: Would you eat the flesh of your dead brother?
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 49:12. Ask: why is the example so strong? It shows how ugly backbiting is. The verse continues: fear Allah; Allah is the Accepting of repentance.

teach.heading: The definition
bullets: Mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes
teach.note: Muslim (Abu Hurairah): the Companions asked, what if what I say is true? He said if it is true you have backbitten, and if it is not, you have slandered him. Discuss examples.

teach.heading: When is it allowed?
bullets: Asking a scholar for a ruling
teach.note: Scholars mention limited cases e.g. a wronged person complaining to someone who can help. Keep short: children should speak to a trusted adult about bullying. Link to safeguarding.

teach.heading: Stopping it
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever defends his brother's honour, Allah will shield his face from the Fire (Tirmidhi, hasan). Practise phrases.

teach.heading: Repair
teach.note: Ask: how can you repair? Make dua and apologise if the person knows. Role-play.

independent: Sort scenarios: backbiting / not backbiting
Write a polite way to leave a gossiping group
Explain 49:12 in your own words
exit: What should you do if you hear it?
lessons.homework: Spend a day avoiding gossip; reflect on any times you succeeded.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with images. Stretch: write advice to a friend who gossips.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: advice, speech and truth online
lessons.title: Adab online: truth, kindness and verification
objectives: Explain verification of news (49:6)
Explain the hadith about narrating all you hear
Apply adab to online learning and messaging

keywords.def: check if something is true
unchecked news
good manners online

teach.heading: The verse
bullets: If a wicked person brings news, verify it
So you do not harm people unknowingly
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 49:6. Ask: how can false news cause harm? Examples from school messages, group chats. Emphasise verifying before sharing.

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: It is enough lying to narrate all you hear
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it is enough lying for a man to narrate everything he hears. Discuss: forwarding messages, screenshots, posts. Link to amanah.

teach.heading: Kind communication
teach.note: Qur'an 49:11: do not mock; do not insult by nicknames. Teams chat rules in school. Review TGA online expectations. Report concerns to a trusted adult.

teach.heading: Privacy and protection
teach.note: Link to amanah and safeguarding. The Prophet ﷺ taught modesty and privacy. Do not require pupils to share personal examples.

teach.heading: My online code
teach.note: Pairs create a three-point code of adab online. Display.

independent: Check three claims: decide how to verify each
Write online adab rules for class chat
Rewrite unkind messages kindly
exit: Name one rule for online adab.
lessons.homework: Show an adult your online code and discuss how to follow it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards and sentence starters. Stretch: write a short guide for younger pupils.

lessons.title: The journey to Ta'if
lessons.bigQuestion: If someone treated you badly and you had the power to punish them, what would you choose?
objectives: To understand what happened at Ta'if and why the Prophet's ﷺ response shows mercy
successCriteria: All: retell the journey to Ta'if in order
Most: describe how the people of Ta'if treated him
Some: explain why he chose mercy instead of revenge

keywords.def: a town in the mountains near Makkah
mercy: kindness and forgiveness
hurting someone back because they hurt you
the Companion who went with him

hook.text: If someone treated you badly and you had the power to punish them, what would you choose?
hook.a: The Prophet ﷺ had that choice at Ta'if and chose mercy and hope.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds' (al-Anbiya 21:107).

starter.q: Who died in the Year of Sorrow?
What does sabr mean?
How long did the boycott last?
Finish: with hardship comes ...

teach.heading: Why Ta'if?
bullets: Makkah grew harder after Abu Talib died
teach.note: Show Ta'if on a map: in the mountains, southeast of Makkah.

teach.heading: A harsh welcome
teach.note: Keep it age-appropriate: the seerah reports he was hurt and his feet bled. He rested in a garden and made du'a.

teach.heading: The angel of the mountains
bullets: Allah sent the angel of the mountains
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim report he said he hoped Allah would bring from their children people who worship Allah alone. Later, the people of Ta'if did become Muslim.

check.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ choose for the people of Ta'if?
options: Mercy and hope for their children
check.why: He refused the offer to destroy them and hoped their descendants would worship Allah.

teach.heading: Mercy to the worlds
teach.note: Ask: which choice leads to good later?

practice.q: Put in order: angel's offer, stones thrown, walk to Ta'if, du'a in the garden.
practice.a: Walk to Ta'if, stones thrown, du'a in the garden, angel's offer
practice.model: First the walk to Ta'if with Zayd. Then the leaders refused and stones were thrown. Next he rested and made du'a. Then the angel of the mountains came.

practice.q: Who went with him?
practice.a: Zayd ibn Harithah

independent.q: In the portal response box, write a letter from Zayd to a friend describing Ta'if and the Prophet's ﷺ choice. Start: 'Dear friend, today we ...'
independent.a: Describes the journey, the stones, the angel's offer and the choice of mercy.
independent.model: Teacher writes: 'Dear friend, today we walked into the mountains to Ta'if, hoping they would listen ...'

independent.q: Extend: what happened to the people of Ta'if later?
independent.a: They became Muslims.

independent.q: Stretch: how can you show mercy when someone is unkind to you?
independent.a: For example: not hitting back, making du'a for them, being kind.

exit.q: Ta'if is ...
exit.a: A town in the mountains near Makkah
options: A town in the mountains near Makkah

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what did the Prophet ﷺ choose, and why?
exit.a: Mercy, hoping their children would worship Allah.

lessons.title: The rules of fasting: intention, what breaks it and who is excused
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it fair that some people do not have to fast? Why might Allah allow it?
objectives: To understand the main rules of sawm and how Islam makes fasting easy for those who cannot
successCriteria: All: say what niyyah is for the fast
Most: sort things that break or do not break the fast
Some: explain who is excused and what they do instead
lessons.smsc: Moral: ease, fairness and care for those who cannot fast

keywords.def: intention in the heart
allowed not to do something because of a good reason
making up a missed fast later
feeding a poor person for each fast someone can never make up

hook.text: Is it fair that some people do not have to fast? Why might Allah allow it?
hook.a: Yes: Allah wants ease for us (2:185). The ill and travellers make it up later.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship' (al-Baqarah 2:185).

starter.q: Sawm lasts from ... to ...
The meal at sunset is ...
Which ayah says fasting was decreed?
What is taqwa?
starter.a: Being aware of Allah and careful to obey Him

teach.heading: Niyyah
bullets: Intend in your heart to fast
teach.note: Link to 'actions are by intentions' (Bukhari 1). The intention is in the heart.

teach.heading: Breaks it, or not?
teach.note: Pupils show 1 (breaks) or 2 (does not break). Explain forgetting: Bukhari and Muslim report Allah fed him, so the fast continues.

teach.heading: Who is excused?
teach.note: Read al-Baqarah 2:184-185 in summary: the ill and travellers make up the days.

head: Who
What they do
rows: Fidyah: feed a poor person each day
Not yet required; may practise part days

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Aisha forgets and drinks juice while fasting. What happens?
check.why: Eating or drinking by mistake does not break the fast (Bukhari and Muslim).

practice.q: Explain what a traveller does about fasting in Ramadan.
practice.a: They may leave the fast and make up the days later.
practice.model: Allah allows the traveller not to fast (2:184). He counts the days missed. After Ramadan he fasts the same number: this is qada'.

practice.q: Swallowing water on purpose ...
practice.a: Breaks the fast

practice.q: What is fidyah?
practice.a: Feeding a poor person for each fast someone can never make up

independent.q: Answer three 'Ask the teacher' letters (in the portal response box): 1) I am ill; 2) I forgot and ate; 3) My grandad is too old to fast. Start: 'Dear ..., Islam teaches ...'
independent.a: 1) Rest; make up the fast later. 2) Your fast continues. 3) He gives fidyah: feeds a poor person for each day.
independent.model: Teacher answers letter 1: 'Dear Yusuf, Islam teaches that if you are ill you may leave the fast and make it up when you are well (2:184).'

independent.q: Extend: why is there no special sentence for the niyyah?
independent.a: Intention is in the heart.

independent.q: Stretch: what does 'Allah intends for you ease' (2:185) teach about Islam?
independent.a: Islam does not ask more than we can bear; it is merciful.

exit.q: Who must make up missed fasts later?
exit.a: Someone who was ill

exit.q: Back to our ponder: why does Allah excuse some people?
exit.a: Allah wants ease for us; they make it up or give fidyah.

lessons.title: Reflecting on Ramadan and zakat al-fitr
lessons.bigQuestion: Ramadan has ended. What one habit from Ramadan do you most want to keep, and why?
objectives: To understand what zakat al-fitr is, who gives it and why it is given before the Eid prayer
successCriteria: All: say what zakat al-fitr is
Most: explain who pays it and when
Some: explain how it purifies the fast and helps the poor
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: reflection; Social: sharing the joy of Eid with the poor

keywords.def: the charity of breaking the fast, given at the end of Ramadan
a measure of food, about four double handfuls
think back carefully
the celebration after Ramadan

hook.text: Ramadan has ended. What one habit from Ramadan do you most want to keep, and why?
hook.a: Pupils' own: for example reading Qur'an daily; good habits please Allah when they last.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays' (al-A'la 87:14-15).

starter.q: Bismillah. Sawm lasts from ... to ...
Who is excused from fasting and makes it up later?
What was given in the Mi'raj?

teach.heading: Looking back on Ramadan
teach.note: Pupils type one thing in the chat for each branch.

teach.heading: What is zakat al-fitr?
bullets: A sa' of food for every Muslim
Young and old, given by the head of the family
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet ﷺ made zakat al-fitr a duty: a sa' of dates or barley on every Muslim, young and old, given before people go out to the Eid prayer (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Why give it?
bullets: It makes up for small mistakes in our fast
The poor can celebrate Eid too
teach.note: Scholars explain its purpose this way: purifying the fast and feeding the poor.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: When must zakat al-fitr be given?
check.why: It is given before people go out to the Eid prayer (Bukhari and Muslim).

practice.q: Explain why zakat al-fitr is given before the Eid prayer.
practice.a: So poor families have food in time to celebrate Eid with everyone.
practice.model: Point: it must reach the poor in time. Evidence: the Prophet ﷺ said to give it before the Eid prayer (Bukhari and Muslim). Explain: poor families can then enjoy Eid. Link: it shows care for the whole community.

practice.q: Who is zakat al-fitr paid for?
practice.a: Every Muslim, young and old

practice.q: A sa' is a measure of ...
practice.a: Food

independent.q: Write a short Ramadan reflection in the portal response box: one thing you did well, one habit to keep, and one sentence on how zakat al-fitr helped others. Start: 'This Ramadan I ...'
independent.a: Personal reflection with a habit to keep and a correct sentence on zakat al-fitr
independent.model: Teacher writes: 'This Ramadan I read a page of Qur'an each day. I will keep this habit after Ramadan.'

independent.q: Extend: name two foods given as zakat al-fitr in the Prophet's ﷺ time.
independent.a: Dates and barley

independent.q: Stretch: why does a baby also have zakat al-fitr paid for them?
independent.a: It is due on every Muslim, young and old; the family pays it.

exit.q: Zakat al-fitr is paid ...
exit.a: At the end of Ramadan, before Eid prayer
options: At the end of Ramadan, before Eid prayer

exit.q: Back to our ponder: which habit will you keep, and how?
exit.a: Pupils' own habit with a plan

lessons.unit: Spring 2: The pledges at Aqabah, the Hijrah and zakah
lessons.title: The Hijrah: the plan, the cave of Thawr and Abu Bakr as-Siddiq
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it enough to trust Allah without making a plan? What did the Prophet ﷺ do?
objectives: To understand how the Prophet ﷺ planned the Hijrah and trusted Allah in the cave of Thawr
successCriteria: All: put the events of the Hijrah in order
Most: explain how careful planning and trust in Allah went together
Some: explain what 9:40 teaches about trust
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: distance and routes on a map (Makkah to Madinah)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: tawakkul; Moral: loyalty and courage

keywords.def: the migration from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE
the mountain cave where they hid for three days
the truthful: Abu Bakr's title
trusting Allah after doing your best

hook.text: Is it enough to trust Allah without making a plan? What did the Prophet ﷺ do?
hook.a: No: he planned carefully and then trusted Allah completely.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'If you do not help him, Allah has already helped him ... when he said to his companion, Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us' (at-Tawbah 9:40).

starter.q: Bismillah. How many pledges were there at Aqabah?
Who taught Islam in Yathrib?
What does Ansar mean?

teach.heading: The plot and the plan
bullets: The Quraysh plotted to kill him (8:30)
Abu Bakr prepared camels and a guide
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Read al-Anfal 8:30 in translation.

teach.heading: The journey in order
teach.note: Use a map of Makkah to Madinah (about 450 km).

timeline.label: 3 days
timeline.text: Hide in the cave of Thawr

timeline.label: Food
timeline.text: Asma' bint Abi Bakr brings food

timeline.label: Route
timeline.text: A guide takes a coastal path

teach.heading: In the cave
teach.note: Abu Bakr feared they would be seen; the Prophet ﷺ answered with calm trust (Bukhari and Muslim).

quote.text: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Who slept in the Prophet's ﷺ bed?
check.why: Ali stayed behind; Abu Bakr travelled with the Prophet ﷺ.

practice.q: Explain how the Hijrah shows planning and trust together.
practice.a: They planned camels, a guide, food and a hiding place, then trusted Allah in the cave (9:40).
practice.model: Point: the Prophet ﷺ planned and trusted. Evidence: camels, a guide and the cave were arranged; in the cave he said 'Allah is with us' (9:40). Explain: tawakkul means doing your best and relying on Allah. Link: we plan for exams and still make du'a.

practice.q: How long did they hide in the cave?
practice.a: Three days

practice.q: Who brought them food?
practice.a: Asma' bint Abi Bakr

independent.q: Make a Hijrah timeline on the pupil PDF (six events), then write in the portal response box how one event shows tawakkul. Start: 'Tawakkul means ... For example, ...'
independent.a: Six events in order; tawakkul explained with the cave or the plan
independent.model: Teacher places event 1: 'The Quraysh plot to kill the Prophet ﷺ (8:30).'

independent.q: Extend: why is Abu Bakr called as-Siddiq?
independent.a: He always believed the Prophet ﷺ and was truthful.

independent.q: Stretch: why did the Muslims later start their calendar from the Hijrah?
independent.a: It began the first Muslim community and state.

exit.q: The Hijrah was in ...
exit.a: 622 CE

exit.q: Back to our ponder: is trust enough without a plan?
exit.a: No: plan carefully, then trust Allah.

lessons.homework: Plan one task this week (homework, tidying) step by step, then say 'tawakkaltu 'ala Allah' (I trust Allah) before you start.

greet someone gladly

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what would you build first, and why did the Prophet ﷺ choose a masjid?

lessons.smsc: Moral and social: fairness and caring for those in need

keywords.def: the poor: people with very little
the needy: people who cannot meet their needs
any charity or good deed given freely
the person who receives

hook.text: If you had money to give, who should get it first? How would you decide?
hook.a: Allah tells us in 9:60 exactly who may receive zakah; sadaqah can go to anyone in need.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Zakah is only for the poor and the needy and those employed to collect it and for bringing hearts together and for freeing captives and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the traveller: an obligation from Allah' (at-Tawbah 9:60).

practice.q: Explain two differences between zakah and sadaqah.
practice.a: Zakah is compulsory at 2.5% on savings above nisab for the eight groups; sadaqah is voluntary, any amount, to anyone.
practice.model: Point: zakah is a duty, sadaqah is a choice. Evidence: zakah is a pillar; sadaqah is any good deed. Explain: zakah has a set amount and set recipients (9:60). Link: both please Allah.

practice.q: Name three of the eight groups.
practice.a: For example: the poor, the needy, the traveller

independent.q: Zakah quiz and case cards on the pupil PDF: decide whether each person may receive zakah (example cases), then write a sadaqah plan for your week.
independent.a: Correct decisions using 9:60; a realistic sadaqah plan
independent.model: Teacher does case 1: 'A family who cannot pay for food: yes, they are among the poor and needy.'

independent.q: Extend: why does Allah list the recipients Himself?
independent.a: So zakah reaches the right people fairly.

independent.q: Stretch: name one good cause that could be 'in the way of Allah'.
independent.a: For example: spreading knowledge of Islam (scholars differ on what is included)

exit.q: Zakah is ...
exit.a: Compulsory

exit.q: Back to our ponder: who should get it first?
exit.a: Those Allah names in 9:60, such as the poor and needy.

lessons.homework: Carry out your sadaqah plan this week. (Short zakah quiz and Hijrah timeline check next lesson.)
